newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Perwaja steels itself.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Perwaja steels itself.

text.p: Malaysian steelmaker Perwaja Terengganu Sdn Bhd is in the market with a US$400 million five-year floating-rate note (FRN), bankers said on Thursday.
According to a co-arranger, the FRNs were launched at two levels, both offering a participation fee of five basis points.
The deal may benefit from uncertainty generated by the flotation -- and devaluation -- of the Thai baht this week.
Thailand's sovereign Yankee bond due in 2007 tightened in to 92-95 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries in New York trade from the 105 basis-point level
The Bank of Thailand announced on Wednesday that it would allow its currency to fluctuate under a managed float system, with its value to be determined by market forces.
Thai banks, frequent visitors to the debt market, mainly for floating-rate U.S. dollars, are likely to be most affected in the short-term, bankers said.
However, longer-term the flotation and recent downgrade of Thailand may ultimately eliminate much of the nervousness over the currency and issues by Thai borrowers.

In other news, bankers said early indicative pricing for Indian Railway Corp's US$100 million seven-year FRN pointed to par issue price, and a coupon of 75 basis points over the Six Month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).

ANZ Investment Bank is lead manager for the deal which has no calls or puts, and indications are that senior lead managers with US$10 million would get 37.5 basis points for an all-in yield of 80.35 basis points.

Lead managers with US$7.5 million get 32.5 basis points or an all-in of 79.64 basis points and senior managers with US$5 million get 27.5 basis points or an all-in of 78.92 basis points. The issue will be priced on July 21.
A HK$6.5 billion term loan facility to redevelop the former Shiu Wing steel mill site in Hong Kong has been launched.
The four-year facility is guaranteed by Swire Properties Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, and was launched through a special-purpose company, Arrowtown Assets Ltd.
It pays a margin of 50 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Everbright Finance and Investment Co Ltd's US$1.05 billion loan facility to help fund its purchase of a stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd has been allotted.
Korea's Housing and Commercial Bank has mandated four banks to arrange a US$150 million three-year floating-rate notes issue, including put and call options at years one and two.
Road King Infrastructure Ltd's issue of notes due 2007 has been increased to US$140 million from US$100 million, after a good response from investors, bankers said.
It was issued at 99.423 with a 9.5 percent coupon to yield 9.591 percent, 312.5 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury.
